housing: Amber Valley mixes former mining and mill towns (Ripley, Alfreton, Heanor) with the stone-built Derwent valley around Belper and rural villages towards the Peak District. Homes are mostly owner-occupied, and private renting is below the England average. Rented homes are typically Victorian brick terraces and ex-council semis in the eastern towns, and stone cottages in the villages. Houses are cheaper than the England average, and new estates have been built on the edges of the main towns.
checkinTips: Stone cottages in Belper, Crich and the Derwent valley: photograph walls and window reveals for damp, and note the condition of any open fire or stove.
Victorian brick terraces in Ripley, Heanor and Alfreton: photograph back yards, outhouses, rear doors and the condition of shared alleys and gates.
Rural homes off the mains gas network may have oil tanks or LPG: photograph the tank, its gauge level and any bunding.
Mill-town terraces on steep streets: photograph cellar steps, cellar walls and any signs of water getting in.
Ex-council semis: photograph uPVC windows and doors, their locks and the number of keys, and any garden fences and sheds.
tenantHelp: Tenants in Amber Valley can contact the borough council's private sector housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in a rented home.
